LOBBYING AND POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS POLICY

Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc.
Approved by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee on February 10, 2026
Applies to: every director, officer, employee, and any third party engaged to act for the Company

1. PURPOSE. This Policy governs how the Company engages with government officials, how it makes or withholds political contributions, and how it reports both. It exists because a lobbying contact or a contribution made without approval can create personal criminal liability and can disqualify the Company from government business.

2. NO CORPORATE POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS. The Company makes no contribution of money, property, services, or anything of value to any candidate for federal, state, or local office, to any political party, or to any political committee, whether directly or through a trade association or other intermediary. Federal law prohibits corporate contributions in connection with a federal election, 52 U.S.C. § 30118, and this Policy extends that prohibition to state and local elections regardless of what state law permits.

3. PERSONAL POLITICAL ACTIVITY. You may participate in the political process on your own time and at your own expense. You may not use Company funds, facilities, letterhead, email, or work time for it, and you may not suggest that a personal position is the Company's. The Company will not reimburse a personal contribution in any form, including through a bonus or expense report.

4. PAY-TO-PLAY. Before making any personal contribution to a state or local candidate or official with authority over the award of contracts to the Company, a covered employee must obtain written pre-clearance from the Compliance Officer. This applies to contributions by a spouse or dependent child. A contribution made without pre-clearance can disqualify the Company from state and local business for up to two years and may require the contribution to be returned.

5. LOBBYING REGISTRATION AND REPORTING. Any contact with a federal legislative or executive branch official intended to influence legislation, regulation, or the award of a contract must be reported to the Compliance Officer within five (5) business days. The Company registers and files quarterly LD-2 reports and semi-annual LD-203 certifications under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, 2 U.S.C. § 1601 et seq., where the registration thresholds are met, and tracks time and expenses for that purpose. State and local registration is handled the same way under the applicable state statute.

6. GIFTS AND MEALS TO OFFICIALS. No gift, meal, travel, entertainment, or thing of value may be given to any government official without the prior written approval of the Compliance Officer. Many jurisdictions set the limit at zero, and the federal gift rules for congressional staff are stricter than the Company's general gift policy.

7. OUTSIDE LOBBYISTS AND CONSULTANTS. Any third party retained to contact a government official on the Company's behalf must be approved in advance, must contract in writing to comply with this Policy and with the Lobbying Disclosure Act and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, must certify compliance annually, and may not be compensated on a contingency tied to a government decision.

8. TRADE ASSOCIATIONS. Before joining or renewing membership in any trade association, the Compliance Officer will obtain a written statement of the portion of dues used for lobbying or political activity, will report that portion to the Committee annually, and will opt out of any political use of dues where the association permits it.

9. FOREIGN OFFICIALS. Nothing in this Policy permits any payment to a foreign official that the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act prohibits. The Company's Anti-Bribery Policy governs, and its prohibition on facilitation payments applies without exception.

10. RECORDS. Every approval, report, and registration under this Policy is recorded accurately in the Company's books, and no such payment may be recorded in a way that obscures its nature or recipient.

11. REPORTING AND NON-RETALIATION. Report a suspected violation to the Compliance Officer or to the anonymous ethics line at 1-800-555-0143. The Company prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith, and nothing in this Policy limits your right to report to a government agency.

12. DISCIPLINE. Violation of this Policy may result in discipline up to and including termination and in referral to law enforcement.

13. OVERSIGHT AND REVIEW. The Compliance Officer reports lobbying expenditures, political activity, and trade-association dues to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee at least annually. This Policy is reviewed annually.
